title: Urban congestion relief experiments through routing-app interventions
actual_jurisdiction: Multi-jurisdiction (10 US Metros: Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, Miami, New York, Philadelphia, Salt Lake City, San Francisco, Seattle)
target_location: Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, Miami, New York, Philadelphia, Salt Lake City, San Francisco, Seattle
factual_summary: Google Research and academic co-authors conducted randomized switchback routing experiments across approximately 100 congested arterial and highway segments in 10 major US metropolitan areas. By rerouting a small share of Google Maps navigation requests to alternative routes of equivalent road classification and comparable travel times, the intervention achieved a city-average 2% increase in vehicle speeds on intervened segments, a 0.7% improvement in city-average travel times, and projected annual CO2-equivalent emissions savings exceeding 1,000 tons per city.

title: City Council Approves Pilot Program to Curb Waze Traffic on Side Streets
publisher: NBC Los Angeles (KNBC) / City News Service
factual_summary: On April 30, 2019, the Los Angeles City Council unanimously voted (12-0) to approve a pilot program authorizing city officials to condition future municipal data-sharing agreements with navigation application developers (such as Waze) on commitments to restrict algorithmic routing of vehicles onto small residential side streets.

title: New Jersey Town Closes Some City Streets to Drivers Who Don’t Live There
actual_jurisdiction: Borough of Leonia, Bergen County, New Jersey
factual_summary: On January 22, 2018, the Borough of Leonia, New Jersey, closed 60 municipal streets to non-resident drivers during peak morning (6-10 AM) and evening (4-9 PM) rush hours, backed by yellow resident car tags and a $200 fine. The measure aimed to halt massive navigation-app traffic diversion heading to the George Washington Bridge. While Waze agreed to display the closures as restricted access, legal authorities and critics challenged the legality of privatizing public streets.

title: Delridge Neighborhood Greenway | 26th Ave SW Proposed Diverters: Outreach Summary
factual_summary: Following the removal of bike lanes on Delridge Way SW for the RapidRide H Line transit project, SDOT proposed installing curb-and-post traffic diverters at SW Brandon St and SW Genesee St along 26th Ave SW to prevent vehicle cut-through traffic on the neighborhood greenway. After initial notification in July 2020, intense neighborhood backlash prompted SDOT to halt construction on July 28, 2020 and conduct a public outreach process (293 survey responses, 32 meeting participants). The community overwhelmingly rejected the diverter options, citing loss of neighborhood access and fears that traffic would merely divert to 25th Ave SW.

title: Waze Connected Citizens Program - United States - Waze Discuss
actual_jurisdiction: Multi-jurisdiction / United States (Inaugural partners: Boston, Los Angeles County, NYPD, Florida DOT, Utah, Kentucky)
target_location: Boston, Los Angeles County, Miami, New York City, Pittsburgh; Florida, Utah, Kentucky
factual_summary: On the Waze Discuss map editor community forum, community leadership and Waze coordinators presented the Waze Connected Citizens Program (CCP), a free two-way data-sharing partnership between Waze and municipal/state transportation agencies. Municipalities supply authoritative road closure, construction, and incident feeds, while Waze provides real-time driver incident and congestion telemetry. Volunteer map editors coordinated outreach templates to onboard departments of transportation across the United States.

title: Communication from Public: Council File #11-2130-S4 (Rowena Ave / Angus St Cut-Through Mitigation)
publisher: Los Angeles City Clerk / Silver Lake Neighborhood Council
actual_jurisdiction: City of Los Angeles, California (Silver Lake, Council District 4)
factual_summary: Official Community Impact Statement and public comment letters submitted to the Los Angeles City Council regarding Council File 11-2130-S4. Silver Lake stakeholders and the neighborhood council testified that while the Rowena Avenue road diet improved arterial safety, cut-through traffic spilled over onto adjacent residential streets, producing treacherous speeding conditions on Angus Street and Waverly Drive. The neighborhood council unanimously (18-0) demanded that LADOT convert Angus Street to a one-way westbound corridor.

title: Lawmaker warns of proposal that could alter California drivers' commutes: 'Adds 30 minutes'
factual_summary: News coverage of legislative debate surrounding California Assembly Bill 2015. While proponents led by Assemblymember Buffy Wicks aim to address commuter bypass traffic flooding residential streets, conservative lawmaker Carl DeMaio warns that state intervention in navigation app algorithms could add 30 minutes to daily commutes by restricting detour routes.

title: Motion 14-1741-S1 (Data-Sharing Partnership with Waze to Protect Residential Streets)
factual_summary: Official Los Angeles City Council motion introduced by Paul Krekorian and Tom LaBonge directing LADOT to report on data-sharing partnerships with Waze. The motion emphasizes leveraging municipal traffic feeds while establishing protocols to prevent navigation apps from diverting heavy cut-through traffic onto quiet residential hillside streets.

title: L.A. May Crack Down on Waze and Google Maps
factual_summary: Los Angeles City Council approved a pilot program directing the city attorney and LADOT to draft data-sharing agreements requiring navigation app developers to keep commuter traffic off narrow hillside and residential streets as a condition of receiving city road closure and incident data.

title: Waze Hijacked L.A. in the Name of Convenience. Can Anyone Put the Genie Back in the Bottle?
factual_summary: In-depth investigative feature detailing the battle between Los Angeles neighborhoods and navigation apps. Chronicles severe cut-through gridlock in Echo Park (Baxter Street crashes) and Silver Lake, resident guerrilla tactics (reporting fake accidents and construction on Waze), speed hump installations, and the legal constraints preventing cities from closing public streets to non-residents.

title: Waze restricted due to buildup of side street traffic in Los Angeles
publisher: ABC 10News San Diego / City News Service
factual_summary: Broadcast reporting on the Los Angeles City Council's vote approving a pilot program to restrict vehicle routing onto residential side streets as a prerequisite for data-sharing agreements with navigation app developers like Waze and Google.

title: 'Absolute chaos': Navigation apps blamed for traffic nightmare on one of L.A.'s steepest streets
actual_jurisdiction: City of Los Angeles, California (Echo Park)
factual_summary: Coverage of dangerous traffic conditions on Baxter Street in Echo Park, one of the steepest roads in Los Angeles (32% grade). Residents attribute a surge in spinouts, rollovers, and crashes to navigation apps routing unsuspecting commuters through the hill during peak hours.

title: Walsh announces partnership with traffic app, Waze
factual_summary: Boston Mayor Martin J. Walsh announced a data-sharing partnership with Waze under the Connected Citizens Program. Boston feeds real-time construction and road closure data to Waze, while receiving crowdsourced telemetry to improve municipal traffic management and signal operations.

title: Boston partners with Waze to clear up clogged streets
factual_summary: Technology news coverage of Boston's Connected Citizens partnership with Waze, detailing how city engineers use telemetry from ~400,000 regional drivers to adjust intersection signals at the Traffic Management Center.

title: Using Waze Data to Measure Traffic Congestion
publisher: City of Boston Citywide Analytics Team
factual_summary: Official empirical report by the Boston Citywide Analytics Team evaluating the impact of the Centre Street West Roxbury road safety redesign (road diet) using anonymous, aggregated Waze travel time and jam data from pre- and post-construction periods.

title: MassDOT partners with Waze to improve traffic, planning
factual_summary: MassDOT joins the Waze Connected Citizens Program statewide, providing official highway incident and construction closure information while receiving real-time congestion reports to inform highway operations and future infrastructure capital planning.

title: Wood Street In West Town, Wicker Park Going One-Way To Cut Down On Thru-Traffic
actual_jurisdiction: City of Chicago, Illinois (West Town & Wicker Park, 1st Ward)
factual_summary: CDOT and 1st Ward Alderperson Daniel La Spata converted two sections of Wood Street in West Town and Wicker Park into southbound one-way streets as part of a corridor overhaul designed to stop commuter cut-through traffic, improve pedestrian safety, and add bike infrastructure.

title: Proposal To Make Wood Street One-Way Stirs Debate In West Town
actual_jurisdiction: City of Chicago, Illinois (West Town, 1st Ward)
factual_summary: CBS News reports on intense neighborhood debate over converting Wood Street and Campbell Avenue to one-way streets. Alderperson La Spata asserted residents approved the plan via participatory budgeting, but dissenting neighbors mounted a petition drive with 'Keep Wood a two-way street' signs.

title: Saka Says He Opposed Traffic Diverters In His Neighborhood Because Of Equity Concerns
factual_summary: Seattle City Council Transportation Chair Rob Saka explains his opposition to SDOT traffic diverters on 26th Ave SW in Delridge, arguing that restricting left turns in a historically underserved neighborhood constituted an equity barrier that severed access to grocery stores in an existing food desert.

title: Stop the installation of traffic diverters at SW Genesee and SW Brandon
factual_summary: Community petition signed by West Seattle residents demanding that SDOT halt planned traffic diverters at SW Genesee St and SW Brandon St along the 26th Ave SW greenway, arguing diverters will push traffic onto narrower side streets without sidewalks and delay first responders.

title: Home Zone: Lake City
factual_summary: Official program documentation for the Lake City Home Zone pilot project, outlining a holistic neighborhood traffic calming toolkit including speed humps, painted intersections, chicane diverters, and street trees to deter cut-through traffic.

title: Waze’s Maps Now Change as Roads Close
publisher: The New York Times Bits Blog
factual_summary: New York Times reporting on Waze's launch of real-time crowdsourced road closure reporting. Highlights integration with official DOT data, such as Georgia DOT's 511 system, to instantly adjust navigation routing around closed streets and accidents.

title: Navigation App Waze Adds Road Closure Reporting, Says It Now Has 40M Users
factual_summary: TechCrunch reports on Waze surpassing 40 million users and launching structured road closure reporting with metadata attributes including closure cause (construction, event) and expected duration.

title: Waze Connected Citizens Program Factsheet
factual_summary: Official factsheet detailing the Waze Connected Citizens Program (CCP), an API-based bilateral data exchange providing municipal partners with real-time incident and jam telemetry in return for municipal advance road closure notices.

title: Waze for Cities (W4C) Program Overview
factual_summary: Technical documentation outlining Waze for Cities (formerly CCP), explaining how local governments exchange public incident reports and road closures with the Waze platform and volunteer editing community.

title: Feature Request: Blacklist Areas / Roads
factual_summary: Community proposal submitted by Waze volunteer map editors and drivers requesting a 'Blacklist Areas / Roads' feature to allow excluding specific dangerous, narrow, or resident-only roads from routing algorithms.

title: Waze for Cities - Google Cloud Analytics
factual_summary: Marketing and product page explaining how municipal partners can query historical Waze traffic congestion, pothole, and accident datasets using Google Cloud BigQuery tools.

title: Traffic Control and Routing in the Era of Algorithmic Navigation
publisher: University of California, Berkeley (Doctoral Dissertation of Theophile Cabannes)
factual_summary: Doctoral dissertation examining the mathematical foundations and real-world externalities of algorithmic navigation apps. Empirically and theoretically models cut-through traffic phenomena in Fremont, CA; Los Angeles, CA (Baxter Street crashes); and Leonia, NJ (fatal crash on Ford Lee Road), evaluating game-theoretic traffic equilibria.

title: Data Integration, Sharing, and Management for Transportation Planning and Traffic Operations
factual_summary: National research report outlining frameworks and best practices for integrating commercial third-party navigation vendor data (Waze, INRIX, HERE) into municipal and state transportation planning and real-time operations.

title: Regular Council Meeting Minutes (July 21, 2026)
actual_jurisdiction: Borough of Mantoloking, Ocean County, New Jersey
factual_summary: Official council meeting minutes documenting municipal response to summer shore cut-through traffic. Police Chief reported that previous requests to Google and Waze to stop routing commuter traffic through local residential streets were denied by the companies, prompting the Borough to deploy electronic message boards, extra police staffing, and physical traffic controls.

title: Smart City Challenge Phase II Application
actual_jurisdiction: City and County of San Francisco, California
factual_summary: SFMTA's federal Smart City Challenge grant application detailing a proposed integration with parking analytics vendor Smarking to push real-time BART station parking availability via API to Google Maps and Waze.

title: Citizens Advisory Committee Meeting Packet (September 3, 2025)
actual_jurisdiction: City and County of San Francisco, California
factual_summary: Official meeting packet for SFCTA Citizens Advisory Committee reviewing neighborhood transportation plans and evaluating trade-offs between neighborhood traffic calming versus maintaining transit and arterial throughput.

title: Alphabet's Tesla Robotaxi Rival Waymo Announces Partnership With Waze To Help Cities Fix Potholes
actual_jurisdiction: Multi-jurisdiction (San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin, Atlanta)
target_location: San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin, Atlanta
factual_summary: Waymo and Waze launched a collaborative initiative utilizing Waymo autonomous vehicle perception and vibration/physical feedback sensors to detect road surface potholes during passenger operations. Road hazard and degradation coordinates are transmitted to municipal transportation departments via the Waze for Cities data platform, piloting in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin, and Atlanta.

title: Can Waymo and Waze fix cities' potholes?
actual_jurisdiction: Multi-jurisdiction (San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin, Atlanta)
target_location: San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin, Atlanta
factual_summary: Mashable analysis of the Waymo and Waze pothole-patching pilot. Robotaxis automatically detect pavement flaws and upload them through Waze for Cities to state and local DOTs, while Waze drivers in pilot cities can view and verify pothole markers in-app. Evaluates municipal capacity bottlenecks to repair identified potholes.

title: Esri Helps Bring Up-to-Date Road Closure Information to Google Maps and Waze
factual_summary: Esri expanded its ArcGIS Community Maps Program and Road Closures solution to allow over 100 municipal and county governments to publish authoritative road closure layers directly to Google Maps and Waze via Waze for Cities, while ingesting crowdsourced traffic incidents back into public GIS portals.

title: Esri Partners with Waze Connected Citizens Program to Deliver Unprecedented Open Data-Sharing Options to Governments Partnership Enables More Municipalities around the World to Share and Analyze Waze Traffic Data
factual_summary: Esri formed a foundational partnership with the Waze Connected Citizens Program (CCP) integrating Waze's crowdsourced traffic data feeds and municipal road closure uploads into the ArcGIS cloud platform, allowing cities to synchronize navigation maps without investing in dedicated roadside sensor networks.

title: Waze and Waycare strike data-sharing pact to improve city traffic
actual_jurisdiction: United States (Southern Nevada / Las Vegas, Tampa, Delaware)
target_location: Las Vegas, NV (Southern Nevada), Tampa, FL, Delaware
factual_summary: Waze and traffic intelligence startup Waycare signed a data-sharing agreement to pool crowdsourced Waze incident data with public agency sensors, cameras, and connected vehicles. The integrated platform was piloted in Southern Nevada with the Regional Transportation Commission, expanding to Tampa and Delaware to improve freeway incident response times.

title: The U.S. government wants to regulate Google Maps all other car navigation apps
factual_summary: The Obama administration's proposed federal surface transportation reauthorization bill (GROW AMERICA Act) included statutory provisions empowering NHTSA to regulate vehicle navigation aids, specifically mobile smartphone apps like Google Maps, Apple Maps, and Waze, granting authority to mandate design modifications for distracted driving safety.

title: Stuck in Traffic? Thanks, Obama!: Feds to Regulate Waze, Google Maps, and Other Navigation Apps
actual_jurisdiction: United States (Federal & California state law case study)
factual_summary: Reason Magazine analysis of the federal transportation bill proposal to grant NHTSA oversight over smartphone navigation apps like Waze and Google Maps. Connects federal regulatory ambitions with state-level distracted driving law enforcement, highlighting the California appellate decision People v. Spriggs, which overturned a citation given to a driver for looking at a smartphone map in stop-and-go traffic.

title: Alert system to warn Illinois drivers about traffic risks, remind them of Scott's Law
factual_summary: Illinois State Police and the Illinois Department of Innovation and Technology integrated HAAS Alert's digital alerting service with navigation apps to broadcast real-time warnings to drivers approaching stationary emergency vehicles on highways under Scott's Law (Move Over Law), expanding on an established ISP partnership with Google Public Sector for Waze and Google Maps.
